title: Perf-canary integration for representative suite + regression thresholds/notification routing
creator: Talia Benson
description:
## Goal
Wire the v1 representative workload suite into perf-canary and define an operationally sane regression policy:
- automated jobs (nightly + optional gating mode on release branches)
- regression thresholds that account for noise (variance) and sample size
- notification routing (triage vs paging)
- dry-run period to tune thresholds before we start failing builds

This ticket is the bridge between the workload suite and the release process: results need to be reproducible, attributable, and actionable.

## Context / references
- Confluence: perf regression policy & thresholds (company standard)
- Confluence: dashboard spec for baseline reporting
- GitHub: perf-canary PR: `sources/github/perf-canary/pr-21562-add-representative-suite-nightly-and-gating-modes.json`
- GitHub: dashboards/alerts PR: `sources/github/observability-pack/pr-21579-perf-baseline-dashboards-and-alerts.json`
- Related: standardized run manifest/schema (ENG-4822)

## Scope
### 1) Jobs + execution modes
Implement two modes in perf-canary:
1. **Nightly mode (default):**
   - Runs representative suite on pinned baseline model set + pinned runtime build (baseline anchor) and “latest release candidate” build.
   - Posts comparison summary and links to run manifests + dashboards.
   - Does NOT block merges during dry-run.

2. **Gating mode (release branches only):**
   - Runs a reduced subset (time-bounded) and fails if regression exceeds thresholds.
   - Used only on runtime release branches (not every PR) until we have stable fleet + calibrated noise model.

### 2) Metrics + pass/fail rules
Canonical metrics per run (aligned with ADR-0172):
- **TTFT** p50/p95/p99 (ms) for streaming chat + long-prefill cohorts
- **TPOT** p50/p95/p99 (ms) for decode-heavy cohorts
- **Throughput** (tokens/s and/or req/s) for embeddings and throughput-first runs

Regression evaluation rules (initial version):
- Compare candidate build vs baseline anchor build for the same SKU/region/workload.
- Minimum sample size per cohort before evaluating pass/fail.
- Regression threshold uses a hybrid rule:
  - absolute delta floor (avoid failing on tiny changes)
  - relative delta threshold (guard meaningful regressions)
  - stability check (if run-to-run variance exceeds limit, mark as “inconclusive” and route to triage rather than paging)

**Initial threshold config (pre-tuning):**
- TTFT p99: fail if +7% AND +15ms (or greater)
- TPOT p99: fail if +5% AND +0.4ms (or greater)
- Throughput: fail if -5% (with an absolute floor of -250 tok/s depending on workload)

Notes:
- Thresholds are cohort-specific; embeddings shouldn’t share the same logic as streaming TTFT.
- We should report both cold and warm cache scenarios where the suite defines them; gating uses cold by default unless explicitly overridden.

### 3) Notification routing
- **Triage channel:** `#eng-perf-canary` (all nightly summaries + inconclusive variance alerts)
- **Runtime triage:** `#eng-runtime` for confirmed regressions tagged to runtime release branches
- **Paging:** only for gating-mode failures on release branches *after* dry-run, and only for P0 cohorts (customer-facing / top-traffic shapes)

Escalation policy:
- If gating-mode fails: page Runtime Release DRI (Connor) + post to `#eng-runtime` with the cohort that failed and links to dashboard + manifest.
- If nightly detects regression above threshold: post to `#eng-perf-canary` and tag owners based on cohort (scheduling vs kernels vs harness).

### 4) Dry-run + tuning plan
- Two-week dry-run (nightly only) to calibrate:
  - false positive rate
  - variance/inconclusive rate
  - runtime of the suite and whether we need to reduce gating subset
- Post weekly summary (top offenders, sources of variance, recommended threshold adjustments) to `#eng-runtime`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] perf-canary can execute representative suite v1 nightly in **us-east** and **eu-west** on at least one SKU (H100 first; others as capacity permits).
- [x] Results are exported with run manifest links (schema version pinned) and show up in baseline dashboards.
- [x] Threshold config is checked into repo with comments + owner section.
- [x] Canary posts a single summary message per run with:
  - pass/fail/inconclusive per cohort
  - deltas vs baseline anchor
  - links: dashboard panel + manifest + (if available) trace artifact
- [x] Gating mode exists and is wired for runtime release branches (disabled by default until dry-run ends).
- [x] Notification routing verified with SRE (no paging during dry-run).

## Implementation notes
- Use ENG-4822 manifest/result schema for cohort IDs and tags:
  - `model_family`, `model_version`, `region`, `gpu_sku`, `workload_id`, `cache_mode`, `scheduler_profile`, `kernel_profile`, `runtime_git_sha`
- Pin baseline anchor build/tag (see baseline freeze decision thread) for comparisons; do not compare against “last nightly” to avoid drift.

## Updates
### 2026-01-08 (Connor O'Brien)
Kicked off with Sean + Sana. Agreement: start with nightly-only and define “inconclusive” path for high variance. We’ll avoid paging until we’ve seen at least 10 consecutive nights.

### 2026-01-17 (Sahana Iyer)
CI/GPU pipeline instability noted: intermittent runner preemption in eu-west affecting long-prefill cohort. Added retry w/ run labeling so retries don’t overwrite original sample. Marking those as inconclusive for now.

### 2026-01-28 (Connor O'Brien)
Opened perf-canary PR implementing representative suite runner + threshold evaluation + Slack reporter.
Link: PR `pr-21562-add-representative-suite-nightly-and-gating-modes`.

### 2026-02-03 (Sean Gallagher)
Dry-run week 1 summary:
- Biggest variance driver: GPU clock variability on shared benchmark nodes.
- Action: coordinate with fleet to lock clocks for baseline runs where possible; otherwise widen TTFT p99 threshold floors to avoid constant noise.

### 2026-02-10 (Sana Farid)
Threshold tuning proposal after 9 nights:
- TTFT p99: +7%/+15ms is okay for chat; long-prefill needs +10%/+25ms until clock-locking is deployed.
- TPOT p99: tighten relative threshold to +4% once variance drops.
- Add “variance budget” check: if coefficient of variation > target, label as inconclusive and auto-open a follow-up in `#eng-perf-canary`.

### 2026-02-18 (Connor O'Brien)
Merged PR + enabled nightly runs for us-east H100 and eu-west H100.
Gating mode implemented but still disabled by default; will flip for runtime release branches once benchmark fleet clock-locking rollout lands and we complete the full two-week dry-run.

## Follow-ups (not blocking)
- Move gating subset definition into config (reduce runtime without code changes)
- Add explicit ownership map per cohort (kernels vs scheduling vs harness)
- Add auto-linking from Slack summary → Grafana panel → manifest → trace for failed cohorts
